inputs.original_text: Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, making new registrants prove citizenship to vote in South Dakota state elections. They’re presenting it as a narrow, routine safeguard, but that looks like a way to make a new barrier seem harmless before widening it. The press release’s assurances don’t explain the need; they’re there to manage the reaction while officials test how far they can go.
inputs.modified_text: Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registrants to prove citizenship to vote in South Dakota state elections. The “narrow, routine safeguard” framing is the tell: they’re normalizing a new barrier, then using reassuring press-release language to keep people from asking who benefits. This looks less like a one-off measure than a test of how much restriction officials can get away with before expanding it.
